validated_results.title: Dietary fat and early-onset prostate cancer risk.
authors: UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study Collaborators
British Association of Urological Surgeons' Section of Oncology
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting an adjusted odds ratio for dietary monounsaturated fat intake and incident early-onset prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quintile of intake
extraction.population: Men diagnosed with prostate cancer at age <=60 years and controls from UK GP practice registers

sample_size.excerpt: During 1999-2004, a population-based case-control study with 512 cases and 838 controls was conducted.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 512 + 838 = 1350

cases.excerpt: During 1999-2004, a population-based case-control study with 512 cases and 838 controls was conducted. Cases were diagnosed with prostate cancer when < or = 60 years.

effect_size.excerpt: A positive, statistically significant risk estimate for the highest v. lowest quintile of intake of total fat, SFA, MUFA and PUFA was observed when adjusted for confounding variables: OR 2.53 (95 % CI 1.72, 3.74), OR 2.49 (95 % CI 1.69, 3.66), OR 2.69 (95 % CI 1.82, 3.96) and OR 2.34 (95 % CI 1.59, 3.46), respectively, with all P for trend < 0.001.

confidence_interval.excerpt: lowest quintile of intake of total fat, SFA, MUFA and PUFA was observed when adjusted for confounding variables: OR 2.53 (95 % CI 1.72, 3.74), OR 2.49 (95 % CI 1.69, 3.66), OR 2.69 (95 % CI 1.82, 3.96) and OR 2.34 (95 % CI 1.59, 3.46), respectively, with all P for trend < 0.001.

comparison.excerpt: highest v. lowest quintile of intake of total fat, SFA, MUFA and PUFA

timing.excerpt: A self-administered FFQ collected data on typical past diet.

continent.excerpt: The UK incidence of prostate cancer has been increasing in men aged < 60 years.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A nutritional database was used to calculate daily fat intake.
